id: 第四章-终点篇-大导寺信辅的前半生-四-学校-p1

en: 第四章-终点篇-大导寺信辅的前半生-四-学校
In Shinsuke's memory, his school life was entirely gloomy.
u.src: 学校生活在信辅的记忆里都是阴暗的。

en: During his university years, apart from a few courses that did not require note-taking, he was not interested in any of his classes.
u.src: 大学时期，除了几门不用做笔记的课程之外，他对其他任何课程都不感兴趣。

en: For him, studying step by step from middle school to high school, and from high school to university, was merely a way of saving himself from poverty.
u.src: 从初中到高中，从高中到大学，一级一级的读书，对他来说只是摆脱贫穷的自我救赎方法罢了。

en: Originally, Shinsuke did not acknowledge this fact during his middle school years, or at least he had never acknowledged it clearly.
u.src: 本来信辅在中学时代并不认可这个事实，至少没有明确认可过。

en: But from middle school onward, poverty began to settle over Shinsuke's heart like a dark cloud.
u.src: 可是，从初中开始，贫穷像乌云一样开始盘踞在信辅的心头。

en: In high school and university, Shinsuke wanted several times to drop out.
u.src: 在高中和大学时，信辅数次想要辍学。

en: But the threat of poverty foretold a bleak future, and so he always gave up the idea of leaving school with ease.
u.src: 但是，贫穷的威胁正预见着灰暗的未来，因此他总是轻易放弃辍学的打算。

en: There was no doubt that he hated school, and he especially hated the rule-bound middle school.
u.src: 毫无疑问，他憎恨学校，特别憎恨规矩特别多的初中。

en: How unbearably shrill and desolate the horn at the school's gatehouse sounded!
u.src: 学校门房的喇叭声无比凄厉啊！

en: How unbearably melancholy, too, were the leafy poplars on the playground!
u.src: 操场上枝繁叶茂的白杨树也无比忧郁啊！

en: What Shinsuke learned at school was only scraps of useless knowledge, such as dates in European history, chemical equations without experiments, the population of some European city, and so on.
u.src: 信辅在学校学到的都是一些无用的小知识，诸如欧洲历史的时间、没有实验的化学方程式、欧洲某城市的人口数量，等等。

en: As long as one applied oneself a little, learning such things was not necessarily painful.
u.src: 只要略微用点心，学习这些知识不一定痛苦。

en: Yet in fact, trying to forget these useless scraps of knowledge was not at all easy.
u.src: 然而，事实上，想忘掉这些无用的小知识却并不简单。

en: In Dostoevsky's Notes from a Dead House, it is written:
u.src: 杜思妥耶夫斯基的《死屋手记》里写过：

en: "If prisoners were forced to perform useless labor, for example:
u.src: “倘若强迫囚犯做无用的劳务，比如：

en: pouring the water from the first bucket into the second, and then pouring the water from the second bucket back into the first,
u.src: 把第一桶水倒进第二个桶里，再把第二桶水倒回第一个桶里，

en: the prisoners would rather kill themselves."
u.src: 囚犯就会宁愿自杀。”

en: In the gloomy school building, beneath the swaying poplars, Shinsuke felt the same spiritual torment that prisoners felt.
u.src: 在灰暗的校舍里，在摇曳的白杨树下，信辅感受到了囚犯所感受的精神痛苦。
不仅仅是这样……

en: Not only that, the people he hated most were also his middle school teachers.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，他最憎恨的也是初中时候的老师。

en: As ordinary people, the teachers certainly were not bad men.
u.src: 身为一个普通人的老师肯定不是个坏人。

en: But because they bore the responsibility of education, and especially because they had the right to punish students, they naturally became tyrants.
u.src: 但是，由于他们承担“教育责任”——尤其是有权利处罚学生，自然他们就会成为暴君。

en: In order to instill their own prejudices into the hearts of their students, they stopped at nothing.
u.src: 他们为了将自己的偏见灌输到学生里心里，不择手段。

en: One of them, an English teacher nicknamed Daruma, often punished Shinsuke on the grounds that he was arrogant.
u.src: 其中一个外号叫“达摩”的英语老师，常常以信辅“傲慢”的理由惩罚他。

en: Yet the reason Shinsuke was considered arrogant was, astonishingly, that he read books by Kunikida Doppo and Tayama Katai.
u.src: 但是，信辅之所以被认为“傲慢”，竟然是因为他阅读国木田独步和田山花袋的书。

en: There was also a Japanese language teacher with an artificial left eye who looked down on Shinsuke because he disliked martial arts and athletic competitions.
u.src: 还有一个左眼装的是义眼的国语老师，以信辅不喜欢武术和运动比赛的理由而看不起他。

en: Several times he mocked Shinsuke by saying, Are you a woman?
u.src: 曾经数次讽刺信辅：“你是个女人吗？”

en: Shinsuke answered him with a question: Are you a man?
u.src: 信辅反问他：“你是个男人吗？”

en: The teacher, of course, punished him for this arrogant attitude.
u.src: 老师对他这种傲慢的态度当然会惩罚。

en: As for the other incidents, one need only reread that book, Records of Not Deceiving Oneself, to know that the humiliations he suffered were beyond counting.
u.src: 其他事情，只要重新读一遍那本《不自欺记》，就能知道他所遭受的屈辱不胜其数。

en: Shinsuke had a very strong sense of pride, and to preserve his self-respect he had no choice but to resist such humiliation.
u.src: 信辅自尊心很强，为了争一口气，不得不反抗这种屈辱。

en: If he had not resisted in this way, he might have come to despise himself like a delinquent youth.
u.src: 如果他不如此反抗的话，他也许会像不良少年般不屑自己。

en: The path by which he strengthened himself can undoubtedly be found in Records of Not Deceiving Oneself.
u.src: 他的自强之道，无疑可以在《不自欺记》中找到——

en: Although I have been branded with many bad names, there are three underlying reasons for it.
u.src: 我虽然蒙上诸多恶名，深究其中的原因有三个。

en: First, he was bookish and physically weak.
u.src: 其一，文弱。

en: A so-called bookish and weak person is one who values mental strength more than physical strength.
u.src: 所谓文弱的人，也就是重视精神力量胜过肉体力量。
其二，轻浮。

en: A so-called frivolous person is someone who dearly loves perfect things beyond practical gain.
u.src: 所谓轻浮的人，也就是钟爱功利之外的完美事物。
其三，傲慢。

en: An arrogant person, so called, is someone who does not thoughtlessly bend their own convictions in front of others.
u.src: 所谓傲慢的人，也就是在他人不前不妄屈自己所信。

ja: いじめたわけではなかった。
en: However, not all of the teachers bullied him.
u.src: 然而，也不是所有的老师都欺负他。

en: Among them, there were teachers who invited Shinsuke to family tea gatherings, and others who lent him English novels.
u.src: 他们之中，也曾有老师招待信辅参加家庭茶会，也有老师借给他英文小说。

en: He still vividly remembered the English translation of A Sportsman's Sketches that he had borrowed when graduating from the fourth year, and he read it through with great delight.
u.src: 他对四年级毕业时借来的一本《猎人笔记》的英译本记忆犹新，满心欢心的阅读完。

en: But bearing the burden of educational responsibility often hindered warm relations between teachers and ordinary people.
u.src: 但是，由于承担“教育责任”常常影响老师和普通人亲切来往。

en: This was because, while accepting their kindness, there also lurked a kind of humble flattery and ingratiation toward their authority.
u.src: 这是因为在接受他们示好的同时，还潜藏着某种对他们权力的卑微的奉承和讨好。

en: Or else there lurked the ugly spectacle of flattering their homosexual tendencies.
u.src: 要不然，就是潜藏着对他们同性恋倾向的奉承丑态。

en: Whenever Shinsuke appeared before them, he always felt blocked and at a loss.
u.src: 信辅每次在他们面前出现的时候，总是感到受阻无所。

en: Not only that, sometimes he would casually go and take cigarettes, or show off about small matters such as having watched a play while standing.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，有时候还会不拘束的去拿香烟，或者显摆自己站着看戏的一些小事。

en: Naturally, they interpreted this behavior as arrogance.
u.src: 他们自然把这种行为解释成傲慢。

en: There was nothing particularly wrong with that interpretation either.
u.src: 这种解释也没什么问题。

en: After all, he was never a student who inspired affection.
u.src: 本来他就不是个招人喜欢的学生。

en: Judging from the old photograph kept at the bottom of a box, at that time he was a sickly boy with a large head out of proportion to his body, but with bright, piercing eyes.
u.src: 从放在箱子底部的旧照片来看，当时是他头很大，是个头和身体很不相称，但眼睛炯炯有神的病弱少年。

en: This pale, sickly boy was always asking tricky questions and taking pleasure in embarrassing his teachers.
u.src: 这个气色不好的病弱少年总是不停的提出刁钻问题，以为难老师为乐。

en: Every time exam results came out, Shinsuke was able to get high marks.
u.src: 每次考试成绩，信辅都能得到高分。

en: But in conduct, he had never received more than six points, the passing mark.
u.src: 但是，操行成绩却都没得过六分（及格分）以上。

en: Whenever he saw the Arabic numeral 6, he could almost hear the teachers sneering in the staff room.
u.src: 他每次看到6这个阿拉伯数字，都几乎能听到老师们在办公室的冷笑声。

en: In fact, it was true that the teachers used his conduct score as a shield and kept mocking him.
u.src: 事实上，老师用操行分数当盾牌，老嘲笑他也是确实存在的。

en: Because of that six, his overall marks could never place him among the top three.
u.src: 他的总成绩因为这个六分，总也无法名列前三。

en: He hated this kind of retaliation, and he hated the teachers who carried it out.
u.src: 他憎恨这种报复行为，也憎恨这种报复行为的老师。

en: By now, no, up to this very day, he had gradually forgotten the hatred he felt then.
u.src: 到现在——不，直到现在，他已经渐渐忘记当时的这种憎恨。

en: Still, a nightmare is not necessarily a misfortune.
u.src: 不过，噩梦不一定就是不幸。

en: At least because of it, he developed a nature capable of enduring loneliness.
u.src: 至少他因此养成了忍受孤独的性情。

ja: しかったかもしれない。
en: Otherwise, the suffering he experienced in the latter half of his life might have been even more painful than it was.
u.src: 不然他下半辈子所经历的痛苦可能比现在更加痛苦。

en: As if in a dream, he became a writer and published several books.
u.src: 他像做梦一样成了一个作家，出版了几本书。

en: Yet all he gained was desolation and loneliness.
u.src: 然而，他所得到的只有落寞和孤独。

en: Today, when he had already grown used to loneliness, or rather today, when there was no better choice than growing used to it,
u.src: 已经习惯孤独的今天——或者说除了习惯孤独之外，没有更好的办法的今天，

en: looking back over the past twenty years, the middle school building that had once filled him with hatred and pain
u.src: 回忆过去的二十年，那曾经让他憎恨和痛苦的中学校舍，

en: seemed, rather, to be already bathed in a beautiful rose-colored morning light.
u.src: 不如说已经照耀在一片美丽蔷薇色的晨光中了。

en: Only the leafy poplars on the playground remained, with a lonely wind blowing through them...
u.src: 只剩下操场上枝繁叶茂的白杨树，有寂寥的风吹过……
